title: Lower bound on the communication complexity of disjointness
statement: Fix an integer $n \ge 1$, and consider the set-disjointness function on subsets of $[n]$: it takes a pair of subsets $X, Y \subseteq [n]$ — Alice holding $X$ and Bob holding $Y$ — to $\mathtt{true}$ exactly when $X \cap Y = \emptyset$. Then the deterministic communication complexity of this function is at least $n + 1$.
hypotheses_covered: n is a natural number with 1 ≤ n
the function considered is set-disjointness on subsets of [n]
replaced:
For $n \ge 1$, the deterministic communication complexity of $\mathrm{disjointness}(n)$
is at least $n + 1$.
